description: A contemporary residential exterior entrance photographed at standing eye-level with a normal lens, capturing a three-quarter corner view of the front entry facade at dusk. The house features a dramatic mix of materials: a prominent stacked ledge-stone column in pale silver-grey and ivory tones rises from the entry porch, contrasting with matte flat black wall cladding panels on the flanking sections. The roofline overhang is finished in warm honey-toned tongue-and-groove wood planking, providing an organic warmth against the dark exterior. The entry door is a dark matte black panel door with a tall full-height sidelite in black-framed glass with a stainless bar pull, set into a vertical slat black surround. To the right, large black-framed floor-to-ceiling windows reflect the deep orange and pink sunset sky. The porch floor is a smooth large-format light grey concrete or limestone slab. At the base of the stone column sits a dark matte square planter holding a neatly clipped globe boxwood topiary, and a matching conical-form evergreen topiary stands at the left foreground. A wall-mounted matte black fixture with a cage-like open frame and frosted white glass panel emits a warm amber glow from its face, illuminating the stone column surface around it with soft warm wash. The interior through the glazed door glows warm amber-orange. The sky is a dramatic deep peach and purple twilight.
